title: Component lineage registry
description: sources/lineage.yaml: where the items of each evaluation component come from, so the depth ladder can tell independent corroboration from dependent evidence (R-2026-11-02-h, -i, -j, -u). One canonical record per component, not per suite that imports it. Pairwise statuses (independent, dependent, unverified) are derived by build/lineage.py, never written by hand except as a cited `relationships` entry. docs/reference/capability.md, "Component lineage", is normative.

collections.description: Named collections of underlying source examples: the sentences, passages or questions that components draw their items from. Two components whose items come from one collection are dependent (R-2026-11-02-h). A collection is a specific set of examples, such as FLORES-200's sentences or MMLU's questions, never a broad domain or corpus provider such as Wikipedia, which goes in a component's `domains`.

components.description: One canonical record per evaluation component, keyed by the `component` slug that capability.language_coverage entries use.

relationships.description: Explicit, cited pairwise statements for cases the automatic rules cannot resolve, such as a paper that compares two sets directly. An explicit relationship takes precedence over the derived status for the pair it names.

language.description: An ISO 639-3 code, checked against sources/snapshots/language-codes.tsv by build.validate.

task.description: A task class as capability.language_coverage names it, in underscore_form (machine_translation, knowledge_exam).

source.description: One citation, in the shape score records use: a URL, what it showed, when it was read, and the digest of the body read. build.validate checks that the citation is present and well formed; whether it supports the lineage claim is evidence review (R-2026-11-02-j).

lineage_fields.description: The lineage facts a component record, or one of its overrides, can state.

origin.description: original: the component's items were collected or written for it, from a collection of its own. derived: its items come from a parent component or an existing collection (a translation, sample, relabeling or re-host). unknown: no source states where the items came from.

collections.description: The `collections` ids the component's items come from, including its own collection when its origin is original.

parents.description: Components this one derives from. The build follows parents transitively, so a suite that imports SIB-200 is still detected as dependent on FLORES (R-2026-11-02-j).

effort.description: An identifier for the effort that produced the component's text in the language: the translation, writing or annotation work, not the research group. Two components that share an effort are dependent; two components from one group but separate efforts are not (R-2026-11-02-h). null when no source states it.

domains.description: Broad provenance, such as wikinews or news, recorded for readers. Never used to derive dependence: sharing a domain or corpus provider is not enough (R-2026-11-02-h).

curation.description: curated: the record was written from the cited sources. uncurated: a placeholder not yet researched. Both score as unverified when the facts are missing, but the distinction tells evidence work where to start (R-2026-11-02-j).

overrides.description: Language-, split- or task-specific lineage, where a component's upstream source is shared but its translation or annotation effort differs (R-2026-11-02-j). The first override whose selectors all match replaces the fields it states; fields it omits keep the canonical value.

languages.description: When present, the statement holds for these languages only.
